label: NEEDS ATTENTION
means: Something in the project is likely to cause trouble in Snapmaker Orca. For a downloaded 3MF it usually means settings that came from another printer.
why: Studio compares the project's settings with what the U1 and Orca expect. The text on the card says: *The model may be fine; the project settings are the problem.*
do: Read the card's **Do this:** line. For a foreign project it is usually to import the model into a clean U1 project, or to prepare a U1 copy.
Press **Prepare U1 copy** (Preserve creator settings is the safe default) and review the result.
dont: Do not conclude your model is broken: the card says the model may be fine.

label: HEADS UP
means: Worth knowing, often something Studio cannot verify, such as spacing between objects or whether the profile is for a U1.
why: Studio does not yet check spacing between objects in a multi-part layout, and says so rather than guessing.
do: Open the project in Snapmaker Orca and use **Arrange**; watch for collision warnings.
If it says **Profile may not be a Snapmaker U1 profile**, make sure the active printer profile is Snapmaker U1, or prepare a U1 copy.
dont: A heads-up is not a failure; it is a place Studio cannot look for you.

label: STUDIO CAN’T TELL
means: Studio has no way to read this fact from your printer, so it does not guess.
why: Most often no printer is connected. The app's own line says: “Studio can’t tell” means Studio has no way to read that from your printer — not that your printer can’t do it.
do: Connect your printer in Printer Hub to let Studio compare, or
Check the item yourself at the printer; the card says what to check.
dont: Do not read it as “incompatible”. A confirmed problem has evidence in a file Studio can read, such as the printer named in the G-code.

label: STUDIO CAN’T CHECK THIS
means: On a sliced job: the check needs a reading from your printer, such as the toolheads it has, whether the slots are loaded, the bed, or the nozzle fitted.
why: Studio reads the file, not the world. With no printer connected, anything that depends on the machine stays unknown.
do: Connect the printer (Printer Hub) and check the job again, or
Check each item yourself: toolheads, loaded slots, bed, nozzle (the card tells you what to look for).
dont: It is not a failed check. It is a check Studio could not run.

label: LOOKS RIGHT
means: Studio checked this and found nothing wrong.
why: For example, a sliced job that names a U1 reads **Sliced for the machine Studio prepares for**.
do: Nothing to do for this item.
dont: It is advice, not a guarantee. Studio never promises a print will succeed.

label: Needs a fix first
means: The verdict banner on the Workspace: the checks found something worth fixing before you slice.
why: The banner summarises the findings (for example an object off the plate). The **Your fix plan** list underneath says where each step happens.
do: Read the checks, then follow **Your fix plan**: steps marked **Do this in Studio** you can do now; **Do this in Orca** wait for Orca.
dont: A star rating or banner is a summary of the checks, not a verdict on the print.

label: 1 object is outside the U1's printable area.
means: At least one object hangs off the U1's plate. Studio names the object, the edge and the distance, for example *Hangs 55.0 mm past the right edge.*
why: Studio reads where each object sits in the file and compares it with the plate. A small part can pass every size check and still land off the plate.
do: If **Move onto the plate (saves a copy)** is offered, press it, then prepare the moved copy.
If it is not offered, see the placement example in the guide.
dont: Do not conclude the object is too big. Compare its size with how far it hangs over.

label: Moving the objects as one piece would not bring them all on, so Studio will not guess.
means: One shift of the whole layout cannot bring every object onto the plate. Either an object is longer than the plate, or the layout is wider than the plate.
why: Studio moves everything as one piece and verifies the copy, or does nothing. It will not half-fix a project. There is no **Move** button in this case.
do: Open the project in Snapmaker Orca and use **Arrange**, as Studio says.
If one object is longer than the plate, resize, rotate or split it in Orca; Studio does not edit your model.
dont: Do not hunt for a hidden Move button.

label: Studio could not open this file as a 3MF project.
means: The file is damaged, or is not really a 3MF.
why: Studio could not read the 3MF structure. The Workspace can still look normal for such a file, so check Compatibility.
do: Download the file again.
Try it in Snapmaker Orca to see whether it opens there.
dont: Do not trust the Workspace's “Checked” status for a file Compatibility cannot open.

label: Printer not found
means: Studio asked the address and nothing answered, so it checked your project on its own.
why: The printer may be off, on another network, at a different address, or its network interface may be closed.
do: Check the printer is on and on this network.
Check the address is the one the printer shows.
On a U1, turn on Advanced Mode under **Settings → Maintenance** on the touchscreen.
Press **Connect** again.
dont: It does not mean the project is incompatible: with no printer, everything that needs one is marked **Studio can’t tell**.

label: Controls are off until the printer is connected and reachable.
means: Printer Hub's controls are disabled because no printer is connected.
why: That is deliberate: nothing can move the printer until Studio can reach it.
do: Connect the printer in Printer Hub.
dont: It is not an error.

label: Nozzle sizes: not reported
means: The printer did not tell Studio which nozzle is fitted, so Studio does not guess.
why: Printing with a different nozzle than the job was sliced for changes line width and can ruin fine detail, so Studio asks you to check.
do: Check the nozzle on the printer is the size the job was sliced for (the card says, for example, 0.4 mm).
Optionally record it under **Settings → Nozzles**; entries you make are labelled **Confirmed by you**.
dont: It is not a mismatch. It is unknown.

label: Prepare stopped
means: In Project Materials: slots that share one installed preset disagree about vendor or type in the project, and Orca copies a declared value to every slot that uses the same preset.
why: Studio writes nothing rather than copy one slot's vendor or type onto another. The panel names the slots and the conflict.
do: Choose a different preset for one slot, or
remove the declaration in the source project. Studio does not edit it for you.
dont: Nothing was written: your original and any earlier copy are untouched.

label: No spool in your inventory matches this material.
means: Studio found no spool to suggest for that slot.
why: No provider is set up, the provider could not be read, or no spool matches the material.
do: Set a provider under **Settings → Materials provider**, or
choose an installed Orca preset anyway, or press **Keep project's filament**.
dont: It does not block Prepare.

label: Manual check in Orca required
means: You picked a preset you made yourself. Studio can map a spool to it, but cannot confirm Snapmaker Orca will apply its temperature, flow and cooling.
why: In testing, Orca kept the project's own values and showed the preset as modified. Studio therefore does not claim Orca applies them.
do: Check the filament in Orca before slicing.
dont: Do not read it as a failure; read it as a check that is yours.

label: Confirmed by you
means: A fact or preset that you confirmed, rather than one Studio verified or the printer reported.
why: Studio never presents your confirmation as its own proof. It marks what came from you.
do: Nothing; keep it up to date if the printer changes (for example nozzles under **Settings → Nozzles**).
dont: It is not the same as **Proven**.

label: Unverified
means: In the preparation report: Studio could not identify the setting in both files, so it did not call it fine.
why: Studio lists anything it could not identify as unverified rather than assuming it is fine.
do: Look at that setting in Orca before slicing.
dont: It is not an error; it is Studio being honest.

label: What Studio could not carry over
means: Something in the original could not be moved into the prepared copy.
why: Studio prepares only what it can stand behind, and lists the rest.
do: Check that setting in Orca, and set it there if it matters.
dont: Your original is unchanged either way.

label: Install Snapmaker Orca
means: Studio could not find Snapmaker Orca on this computer, so the handoff button reads **Install Snapmaker Orca**.
why: The error text is: “Snapmaker Orca isn’t installed yet — use Install Snapmaker Orca.”
do: Install Orca from its releases page, or press **Copy path** and open the file from Orca if it is installed somewhere Studio did not look.
dont: Studio does not install anything for you.

label: Customized Preset
means: A notice from Snapmaker Orca that the project's settings differ from a system preset.
why: It can appear when the creator's tuned settings are kept, which is what **Preserve creator settings** does.
do: Review the settings in Orca before slicing.
dont: It is Orca's notice, not a Studio error.

label: Sliced for a different printer
means: The sliced job names another machine. Toolpaths, temperatures and machine commands are generated for one specific machine.
why: Studio read the printer named in the G-code. It does not need a printer connected to know this. Sending another printer's job to a U1 usually fails immediately and can crash the toolhead.
do: Re-slice the model in Snapmaker Orca with a U1 profile, and check the new job.
dont: Do not send the job anyway.

label: Studio cannot tie this job to your project
means: Nothing in either file identifies the model, so Studio cannot tell whether this is the slice of the project you checked.
why: The printer and filaments match, but every job sliced on this machine would look like this.
do: Check you picked the right file before you send it.
dont: It is not an error with the job itself.

label: that file does not exist
means: On After Slicing: the path you typed or pasted does not point to a file.
why: A path with a missing folder separator, a moved file or a typo.
do: Copy the exported `.gcode` file's full path again, or drag the file onto the window.
dont: Nothing is wrong with the job.
